title: Schema Tug-of-War: constrained-decoder experiments and recovery playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: quantify and catalog trade-offs when enforcing strict JSON/schema constraints against unconstrained model decoding, and produce a recovery playbook for streaming + tool-calling scenarios. We call this the 'Tug-of-War' suite because it intentionally stresses competing objectives: schema strictness (zero false positives) vs model fluency and latency. Goals: 1) create reproducible stimuli that provoke schema violations in both full and partial streams, 2) measure impact of constrained decoding knobs (sampling temperature, logit penalties, lexicon masks, token-level backoff) on schema pass rate and latency/throughput, 3) validate repair and fallback strategies (repair-by-edit, toolcall re-run, model-variant fallback, short-prefix caching + re-decode), and 4) produce a lightweight runbook for rollout and automated gating in Console.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible test harness (Docker + CI job) that runs the Tug-of-War corpus across at least 3 model families and reports schema pass rate, latency P50/P95, and throughput
Experiment matrix with clear knobs and expected outcomes defined (temperature, top_p, constrained-decoder mode, lexicon mask types)
At least 3 recovery strategies implemented and compared with end-to-end measurements on streaming & interleaved toolcall sequences
Runbook with automatic gating thresholds for Console rollouts and a recommended default decoder configuration for hosted vs Dedicated tiers
